parsed.attack: The author reads openmargin's cause [44] as "too early", but the stated cause has three parts and only one expires with time: "strong competitors" is more true now than in 2014, because Perusall and Hypothesis already occupy line-level social annotation in education and got there through institutions. Readmill, the social e-reader built on shared highlights, was folded into Dropbox and closed in 2014, and Subtext - social annotation built specifically for classrooms around a set text - was absorbed by Renaissance Learning and discontinued. The pattern across all three is that the class-link loop is really a teacher-adoption loop, and teacher adoption is an institutional sales motion, which is exactly where the fourth kill criterion (100 of the first 1,000 sign-ups via a shared class link) will fail the way Subtext failed.
parsed.strongest_defence: A-level and IB set texts are a small, fixed, nationally synchronised list, so the unit is a cohort of students who already sit next to each other rather than an institution to be sold to, and any one student can open the group with a link without the teacher's permission or a procurement cycle.
parsed.verdict_reason: The "too early" half of openmargin's cause has genuinely expired, but the strong-competitor and teacher-adoption halves that closed Readmill and Subtext are fully intact.
